business_data_accuracy_framework.heading: Accurate Excel Reports Begin With Accurate Data
business_data_accuracy_framework.reconciliationRule: Raw Source Total → Formula Summary → PivotTable Total → Management Report. Numbers must reconcile across all layers.
exceptionHandling: Inspect cell data types (numbers stored as text).
Identify missing records and broken lookups.

modern_excel_function_compatibility.targetSoftware: Microsoft Excel for Microsoft 365 (Windows Desktop preferred)
modern_excel_function_compatibility.versionPolicy: Microsoft Excel for Microsoft 365 is the primary classroom software. Newer perpetual versions (Excel 2021/2024) support XLOOKUP and dynamic arrays, whereas older versions like Excel 2016 and 2019 do not natively support XLOOKUP or dynamic arrays.
modern_excel_function_compatibility.fallbackTeaching: For older Excel installations, students learn legacy lookup patterns (INDEX/MATCH and exact-match VLOOKUP) while understanding why modern functions are standard in current office environments.
modern_excel_function_compatibility.dynamicArraySpillRule: Dynamic arrays return multiple values across adjacent worksheet cells. Spill areas must be unblocked. Spilled array formulas cannot live as normal calculated columns inside Excel Tables; tables serve as data sources and standard worksheet ranges receive spilled outputs.

excel_tables_vs_pivottables.excelTable: A structured relational data container supporting column headers, instant filtering, structured references, automatic row expansion, and self-inheriting calculated columns.
excel_tables_vs_pivottables.pivotTable: An analytical calculation engine that summarizes, groups, and cross-tabulates records across rows, columns, filters, and value aggregations.
excel_tables_vs_pivottables.refreshRule: Updating source data in an Excel Table does not automatically refresh connected PivotTables. Students must execute a manual or workbook refresh to recalculate report figures.

power_query_scope.heading: Understand Modern Data Import Without Turning This Into an ETL Course
included: Power Query purpose & Get Data ribbon workflow
Assigning explicit data types (text IDs, currency, dates)
Basic row cleaning (removing empty rows/header junk)
Loading data to an Excel Table or data connection
Refreshing queries upon source dataset changes
excluded: Complex relational merges and append pipelines
Power BI semantic models and DAX modeling

independentVerificationProtocol: 4. Verify data types of referenced cells.

responsible_ai_policy.confidentialityRule: Never upload real HR records, actual employee salaries, personal customer information, or confidential enterprise financial records to unapproved cloud AI tools. Practice exclusively with fictionalized classroom datasets.
responsible_ai_policy.humanAccountability: AI is an assistive drafting tool; the human student remains solely responsible for the mathematical accuracy and integrity of every spreadsheet.

csv_hygiene_policy.heading: CSV Hygiene & File Safety
commonRisks: Leading zeros stripped from numeric IDs, ZIP codes, and phone numbers.
Date formats misinterpreted between MM/DD and DD/MM locales.
Currency symbols causing numeric columns to convert to uncalculable text.
Formula injection risk: external CSV cells beginning with '=', '+', '-', or '@' executing code when opened directly in spreadsheets.
csv_hygiene_policy.safePractice: Inspect data in import preview windows, explicitly set column data types to Text for IDs before importing, and utilize Power Query or the Text Import Wizard rather than blindly double-clicking external CSV files.

curriculum.title: Business Formulas & Functions
curriculum.objective: Apply essential Excel formulas to realistic business reporting problems and independently verify the results.
lessons: 2.1 Formula Fundamentals: Equals sign.; Operators.; Arguments.; Function structure.; Parentheses.
2.2 References in Formulas: Relative.; Absolute.; Mixed.; Copying formulas.
2.3 Basic Functions: SUM.; AVERAGE.; MIN.; MAX.; COUNT.; COUNTA.; Teach as building blocks, not the entire assessment focus.
2.4 SUMIF vs SUMIFS: Conditional sums.; Multiple criteria.; Dates.; Product categories.; Salespersons.
2.5 COUNTIF vs COUNTIFS: Counting records.; Attendance.; Status reports.; Multiple conditions.
2.6 IF: Logical tests.; Business rules.; Status labels.; Eligibility conditions.
2.7 IFS: Multiple conditions.; Ordered tests.; Default cases.; Appropriate use.
2.8 AND / OR: Combined conditions.; Validity checks.; Eligibility rules.
2.9 IFERROR: Handling expected error cases.; Clear messages.; Formula quality.; Important: Do not teach IFERROR as a method of hiding all errors without investigation.
2.10 Lookup Concepts: Unique identifiers.; Lookup tables.; Exact matches.; Missing values.
2.11 XLOOKUP: Lookup value.; Lookup array.; Return array.; Exact match.; Not-found handling.
2.12 XLOOKUP Business Examples: Product price lookup.; Employee department lookup.; Inventory category lookup.; Commission category lookup.
2.13 Duplicate Lookup Keys: First-match behaviour.; Data reliability.; Why identifiers matter.

2.14 INDEX/MATCH Awareness: Concept.; Why older workbooks use it.; Compatibility.; Simple alternative lookup explanation.; Avoid making complex INDEX/MATCH combinations a major advanced specialization.
2.15 VLOOKUP Compatibility Awareness: Recognize existing VLOOKUP formulas.; Understand approximate vs exact match.; Common legacy workbook considerations.
2.16 Text Functions: LEFT.; RIGHT.; MID.; LEN.; TRIM.; CONCAT or TEXTJOIN where supported.; UPPER/LOWER/PROPER.
2.17 Text Cleanup: Extra spaces.; Standardizing codes.; Extracting fields.; Joining text.
2.18 Date Functions: TODAY.; YEAR.; MONTH.; DAY.; EOMONTH awareness.; Date differences.
2.19 Business Date Calculations: Report month.; Attendance month.; Due-date status.; Ageing awareness without advanced finance modeling.
2.20 Common Formula Errors: #N/A.; #VALUE!.; #REF!.; #DIV/0!.; #NAME?.; #SPILL! awareness.
2.21 Formula Auditing: Evaluate Formula.; Trace precedents/dependents.; Formula bar review.; Test cases.
2.22 Formula Verification: Manual calculations.; Small known datasets.; Expected-result examples.; Independent totals.
2.23 Structured References: Table column references.; Automatically filling formulas.; Expanding source tables.
2.24 Business Formula Documentation: Meaning of calculated fields.; Assumptions.; Calculation logic.

1.5 Data Entry: Text.; Numeric data.; Dates.; Percentages.; Currency.; Blank cells.

1.7 Cell References: Relative references.; Absolute references.; Mixed references.; Fill behaviour.
1.8 Basic Calculation: Arithmetic operators.; Order of operations.; Basic formula syntax.
1.9 Essential Formatting: Number formats.; Currency.; Percentages.; Dates.; Decimal precision.

modules.title: Business Formulas & Functions
modules.objective: Apply essential Excel formulas to realistic business reporting problems and independently verify the results.
lessons: 2.1 Formula Fundamentals: Equals sign.; Operators.; Arguments.; Function structure.; Parentheses.
2.2 References in Formulas: Relative.; Absolute.; Mixed.; Copying formulas.
2.3 Basic Functions: SUM.; AVERAGE.; MIN.; MAX.; COUNT.; COUNTA.; Teach as building blocks, not the entire assessment focus.
2.4 SUMIF vs SUMIFS: Conditional sums.; Multiple criteria.; Dates.; Product categories.; Salespersons.
2.5 COUNTIF vs COUNTIFS: Counting records.; Attendance.; Status reports.; Multiple conditions.
2.6 IF: Logical tests.; Business rules.; Status labels.; Eligibility conditions.
2.7 IFS: Multiple conditions.; Ordered tests.; Default cases.; Appropriate use.
2.8 AND / OR: Combined conditions.; Validity checks.; Eligibility rules.
2.9 IFERROR: Handling expected error cases.; Clear messages.; Formula quality.; Important: Do not teach IFERROR as a method of hiding all errors without investigation.
2.10 Lookup Concepts: Unique identifiers.; Lookup tables.; Exact matches.; Missing values.
2.11 XLOOKUP: Lookup value.; Lookup array.; Return array.; Exact match.; Not-found handling.
2.12 XLOOKUP Business Examples: Product price lookup.; Employee department lookup.; Inventory category lookup.; Commission category lookup.
2.13 Duplicate Lookup Keys: First-match behaviour.; Data reliability.; Why identifiers matter.

2.14 INDEX/MATCH Awareness: Concept.; Why older workbooks use it.; Compatibility.; Simple alternative lookup explanation.; Avoid making complex INDEX/MATCH combinations a major advanced specialization.
2.15 VLOOKUP Compatibility Awareness: Recognize existing VLOOKUP formulas.; Understand approximate vs exact match.; Common legacy workbook considerations.
2.16 Text Functions: LEFT.; RIGHT.; MID.; LEN.; TRIM.; CONCAT or TEXTJOIN where supported.; UPPER/LOWER/PROPER.
2.17 Text Cleanup: Extra spaces.; Standardizing codes.; Extracting fields.; Joining text.
2.18 Date Functions: TODAY.; YEAR.; MONTH.; DAY.; EOMONTH awareness.; Date differences.
2.19 Business Date Calculations: Report month.; Attendance month.; Due-date status.; Ageing awareness without advanced finance modeling.

2.21 Formula Auditing: Evaluate Formula.; Trace precedents/dependents.; Formula bar review.; Test cases.
2.22 Formula Verification: Manual calculations.; Small known datasets.; Expected-result examples.; Independent totals.
2.23 Structured References: Table column references.; Automatically filling formulas.; Expanding source tables.
2.24 Business Formula Documentation: Meaning of calculated fields.; Assumptions.; Calculation logic.

portfolio.title: Applied Excel Business Reporting Portfolio
portfolio.objective: Develop and verify 3 practical, production-ready spreadsheet deliverables demonstrating structured data design, business formula calculation, dynamic arrays, PivotTable reporting, and rigorous data reconciliation without relying on advanced BI or VBA macros.
portfolio.countingRule: Three distinct applied deliverables: an Automated Sales Tracker, an Expense OR Attendance Report (student choice), and a comprehensive Final Excel Business Reporting Workbook capstone.

deliverables.title: Automated-Formula Sales Tracker
deliverables.scenario: A sales department needs a reliable workbook to record transactions, calculate sales amounts, and summarize results by product, region, and salesperson.
deliverables.automation_definition: New records entered into an appropriately configured Excel Table inherit relevant calculated-column formulas automatically without VBA macros.
accuracy_tests: Verify sample transaction totals against unit price and quantity multiplication.
Check product lookups against master product catalogue.
Test handling of missing or invalid product IDs.
Add a new record row to confirm automatic formula inheritance.
Reconcile table totals with summary calculations.

deliverables.title: Expense or Attendance Report
deliverables.scenario: Students select ONE operational tracking track (Expense Management or Employee/Student Attendance Monitoring) to produce a verified, formatted departmental register.

option_a_expense_report.required_output: An expense report showing total expenses, category breakdown, department totals, relevant trends, exceptions, and checked totals.

option_b_attendance_report.required_output: An attendance report showing present days, absent days, relevant attendance rate, reporting period, exceptions, and checked calculations.

deliverables.policy: Students submit one complete expense OR attendance report. Both options are explored in classroom practice, but one verified deliverable satisfies the portfolio requirement.

deliverables.title: Excel Business Reporting Workbook
deliverables.scenario: A growing small business requires an end-to-end monthly reporting workbook for executive and operational decision-making.

required_components.a_instructions: Read Me sheet outlining workbook purpose, data sources, reporting periods, update procedures, PivotTable refresh steps, and analytical limitations.
required_components.b_source_data: Properly structured Excel Table with unique column headers, appropriate data types, consistent IDs, and no merged headers.
required_components.c_lookup_reference_data: Lookup tables for products, categories, sales reps, and regions with robust XLOOKUP and reference formulas.
required_components.d_calculations: Summary calculations using SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, IF/IFS, and dynamic arrays where supported.
required_components.e_data_validation: Input validation including restricted drop-down lists, numeric range limits, date constraints, and clear error alerts.
required_components.f_reporting: At least one interactive PivotTable with slicers and at least one clearly labeled business chart highlighting KPIs.
required_components.g_accuracy_checks: Dedicated verification section auditing source row count, duplicate keys, missing IDs, lookup error counts, raw totals, and report reconciliation.
required_components.h_management_summary: Executive commentary summarizing reporting period performance, key metrics, two or more evidence-based observations, limitations, and recommended next steps.

deliverables.documentation: Complete written explanation covering data lineage, calculation formulas, manual refresh triggers, reconciliation methodology, and known constraints.

assessment_model.criticalFailCondition: A report with materially incorrect calculations or unreconciled totals will not receive a passing grade merely because its formatting, color scheme, or charts are visually attractive. Mathematical accuracy and verification integrity are mandatory.

faq.question: What is Microsoft Excel — Business Reporting & Data Analysis?
faq.answer: It is a practical Excel certification covering formulas, structured data, data validation, PivotTables, charts and business reporting.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Six weeks, with 48 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹6,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified fee and tax policy.

faq.question: Is the course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It begins with Excel fundamentals.

faq.question: Do I need prior Excel knowledge?
faq.answer: No. Basic computer and arithmetic skills are sufficient.

faq.question: Which Excel version is used?
faq.answer: Microsoft Excel for Microsoft 365, preferably the Windows desktop version.

faq.question: Will I learn Excel formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, including SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, IF, IFS, IFERROR and XLOOKUP.

faq.question: Will I learn XLOOKUP?
faq.answer: Yes. XLOOKUP is part of the mandatory curriculum.

faq.question: Will I learn VLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH?
faq.answer: Students receive useful awareness of legacy lookup methods, while XLOOKUP is the main modern lookup function.

faq.question: What are dynamic arrays?
faq.answer: They are modern Excel formulas capable of returning results across multiple worksheet cells.

faq.question: Will I learn FILTER, UNIQUE and SORT?
faq.answer: Yes. These are included in the modern Excel module.

faq.question: Why do some formulas not work in older Excel versions?
faq.answer: Modern functions depend on the Excel version. Older installations may lack XLOOKUP or dynamic-array functionality.

faq.question: Will I learn data validation?
faq.answer: Yes, including suitable restrictions and drop-down lists.

faq.question: Will I learn conditional formatting?
faq.answer: Yes, for useful tasks such as highlighting exceptions and business statuses.

faq.question: Will I learn PivotTables?
faq.answer: Yes. PivotTables are a major part of the course.

faq.question: Will I learn charts and reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. Students practise charts, PivotCharts, KPIs and business summaries.

faq.question: Will I learn dashboards?
faq.answer: The course teaches practical reporting summaries with charts and PivotTables, not complex enterprise BI dashboards.

faq.question: Will I learn Power Query?
faq.answer: Yes, at an introductory level for importing and preparing data.

faq.question: Will I learn Power BI?
faq.answer: No. Power BI belongs to an advanced MIS/Business Intelligence pathway.

faq.question: Will I learn VBA or macros?
faq.answer: No. VBA automation is outside this certification.

faq.question: Will I learn Python in Excel?
faq.answer: No. The course concentrates on Excel foundations and applied reporting.

faq.question: Is Copilot required?
faq.answer: No. Copilot is optional and depends on licensing and feature availability.

faq.question: Can AI help with Excel formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, but students must understand and independently verify all formula outputs.

faq.question: What business reports will I create?
faq.answer: A sales tracker, an expense or attendance report and a final Excel reporting workbook.

faq.question: What will my final capstone include?
faq.answer: Structured data, validation, formulas, a PivotTable, charts, quality checks and a management summary.

faq.question: Will I learn CSV import?
faq.answer: Yes, including data types, encoding, dates and common import issues.

faq.question: Will I learn to identify spreadsheet errors?
faq.answer: Yes. Formula errors, invalid data and report reconciliation are important parts of the course.

faq.question: Is this suitable for office executives?
faq.answer: Yes. The content focuses on common office reporting and data analysis work.

faq.question: Can small business owners take this course?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers practical sales, expense and inventory reporting applications.

faq.question: What can I study next?
faq.answer: Suitable progression may include advanced Excel, Business Productivity Mastery and longer MIS/Business Intelligence programs. ---
